To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the acoustic coherence time scales in a continental-shelf environment decay as a power law with range, that this power law is -1/2 in the far field, and that this power law decreases as the internal wave energy increases.

the temporal coherence of an acoustic signal propagating through a random continental-shelf wave-guide is predicted to decay with range as a power law of range with exponent -1/2, and that this power law is consistent with the range dependence observed in the coherence of acoustic signals measured in the continental-shelf environment.

the temporal coherence of acoustic fluctuations after propagating over continental-shelf distances is well predicted by a simple model that accounts for the accumulated effects due to range-dependent multiple forward-scattering by internal waves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the temporal coherence of low-frequency sound in the ocean.
developing a theoretical framework that can be used to predict acoustic coherence time scales in the ocean environment.
the effects of internal waves in ocean acoustics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the temporal coherence of acoustic field fluctuations after forward propagating through a random three-dimensional internal wave field in a continental-shelf environment is predicted to be consistent with the measured coherence time scales.

the acoustic coherence time scales in the continental shelf are controlled by the random fluctuations of the internal waves and that these fluctuations are the dominant source of the temporal coherence of low frequency acoustic field in continental shelf.

a model based on normal mode theory and multiple forward scattering can be used to estimate the temporal acoustic coherence time scale for low frequency sound in a continental-shelf environment with random three-dimensional internal wave energy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the acoustic field coherence time scale is a useful metric for characterizing the acoustic fluctuations due to internal waves, and that it is possible to estimate the coherence time scale of acoustic fluctuations in the ocean from the ocean internal wave statistics.
we have developed and tested a simple model for estimating the temporal coherence of an acoustic signal after propagating through an inhomogeneous medium containing random internal waves.

the temporal coherence of acoustic signals forward propagated through a range-dependent continental-shelf waveguides containing random internal waves can be estimated from the analytical model derived from the normal mode theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the first time, we have developed an analytical model for the temporal coherence of a forward propagated acoustic field that can be used to estimate the coherence time scale as function of the acoustic frequency, range, and internal wave energy in a continental-shelf environment.

the temporal coherence of a narrow-band, low-frequency, acoustic field after propagating through the ocean is a function of the internal wave energy, the range to the receiver, the frequency, and the internal wave spatial scales.
the temporal coherence time scale of the acoustic field in a range-dependent waveguide containing random internal waves decays with a power-law to the -1.5 power with range beyond 1 km.
